first_impression.reaction: My daughter has been saying 'everyone says September' for weeks, so I liked that the first line says no single month suits everyone. And 'how well your guests cope with heat' is in the opening sentence, which is exactly what I'm worried about with Mum. It's sensible and it doesn't talk down to me. I'll read it properly.

journey.quote: The months that work for you depend on four things: the island, how well your guests cope with heat, whether you want a church ceremony, and how long everyone will stay.
journey.reaction: Good. Somebody has thought about the guests, not just the photos. Heat and older relatives is my first question, and it's on the list.

journey.quote: Smartraveller warns that summer heatwaves are frequent in Greece and that wildfires occur from June to September, so high-summer weddings need shade, water and evening timing.
journey.reaction: I trust Smartraveller, and I'm glad it's named rather than glossed over. Wildfires I hadn't even thought of. That goes straight to my husband.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
journey.reaction: I can see they're being careful, but I don't need the years each weather station has been running. This is where I started to skim.

journey.section: Greece wedding weather by month, April to October
journey.quote: Each cell shows the average maximum temperature, then the average number of rain days.
journey.reaction: The table's handy once you get it, and that line explains it plainly. Five columns on the iPad is a squeeze though. I had to turn it sideways.

journey.quote: Smartraveller says wildfires occur in Greece from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations; they can start with little warning and travel quickly, so avoid affected areas and follow local authorities' advice.
journey.reaction: That's a frightening thought with Mum there. The next line says guests should know how to reach the couple, but who is actually keeping an eye on it and moving people if a fire starts nearby? That's what I'd want to know.

journey.quote: For a July wedding, that shapes the day: an evening ceremony, shade for the aperitivo, water at every seat, and shorter excursions for older guests.
journey.reaction: Yes. That's practical and it mentions older guests by name. I can picture Mum in the shade with a glass of water, not stuck on a hot terrace at two o'clock.

journey.quote: The Naxos station records a prevailing north wind in every month, and its wind power reading rises from 10.3 in June to 13.3 in July.
journey.reaction: 10.3 what? I've no idea if 13 is a breeze or a gale. The number means nothing to me, so I just had to take their word that it's windy.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds, so reconfirm departures.
journey.reaction: Good to know, and the buffer day advice later on is sensible. With elderly relatives, a cancelled ferry is the last thing I want.

journey.quote: If yours is in the second half of the month, check the date with your priest before you send save-the-dates.
journey.reaction: My sister-in-law's side is Greek Orthodox, so this matters. I'd never have known 1 to 15 August was closed. That alone could save us a lost booking.

journey.quote: May and late September to October keep maximums in the low to mid 20s at most stations.
journey.reaction: That's my answer, really. Low twenties suits Mum and the aunties. Clear, short, and I can forward that line.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian dollars, the fee in writing before they start. That's the sentence I'd read out to my husband. It sounds accountable.

journey.quote: Ask your venue about water temperature for your month, since the figures in this guide cover air, not sea.
journey.reaction: Honest. They're not pretending to know what they don't. I prefer that to a made-up number.

unanswered_questions: If a heatwave or wildfire hits during the wedding week, who on the planning side watches the warnings and helps move guests?
Can the Wedded Advisor suggest venues with shade, air-conditioned rooms and level access for someone with a walking frame?
What travel and medical insurance should older relatives take out for a summer trip to Greece?
Is the deposit protected, and who checks a contract written in Greek and in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step a phone call with a real person, before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: The Naxos station records a prevailing north wind in every month, and its wind power reading rises from 10.3 in June to 13.3 in July.
turn_offs_found.why: A number with no unit and no explanation. It makes me feel I'm missing something obvious, and it doesn't tell me whether Mum could sit outside. A plain 'strong enough to blow veils and table settings' would do the job.

turn_offs_found.quote: These are long-term monthly averages, not forecasts. The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
turn_offs_found.why: Too technical for me, and it comes early, before the part I actually came for. The first sentence is enough. The station years could sit under the table in small print.

would_share_with: My husband, with the Smartraveller heat and wildfire lines and the Wedded Advisor paragraph (AUD, fee in writing)
My daughter, with the 'Older guests, or anyone who struggles in heat' scenario and the Orthodox closed dates
My sister, who will travel with Mum, with the July line about shade, water and shorter excursions for older guests

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as a single point of contact, anywhere in the world, and confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It says the right things: one person, payments handled, inclusions in writing. I'd click once my daughter has narrowed it to a couple of months, but I'd want to hear from a real person on the phone first, and to know they'll think about Mum's comfort and what happens if the weather turns.

top_3_changes: Explain the Naxos 'wind power reading' (10.3, 13.3, 13.9, 14.5) in plain words, or drop the numbers and say what the wind means on the day (veils, candles, table settings, sitting outside). As it stands I can't tell a breeze from a gale.

After the wildfire and heatwave paragraphs, add one line on how a Wedded Advisor helps in practice (choosing shaded or air-conditioned spaces, keeping guests informed if plans change), so a parent isn't left thinking the couple manages it alone.
Move the station date ranges ('The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010...') below the table as a source note, so the guide gets to the months sooner and reads less like a weather report.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding mother of the bride, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad, sent the link by her daughter)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible

Deferred business details (deposits, contracts, 2am contact, call first) and transfers not raised as must-fix; absence of a single best month, prices, crowd claims and sourcing not raised as problems, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: The unexplained Naxos 'wind power reading' numbers are the main clarity problem for this persona (should-fix). A parent also wants one line on how the Wedded Advisor helps during a heatwave or wildfire, beyond 'guests should know how to reach you' (medium). Station date ranges early on are a minor readability turn-off. Older guests are well served by the July and scenario sections. Deposits, contract language, 2am contact, insurance and call-first are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret's daughter is the bride and sent the link; Margaret's mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples) and some family members are Greek Orthodox, which is why the church dates mattered to her.
No single best month, no prices and no crowd claims are by design, and the brand does not discuss sourcing, so none were raised.
